kata.name: Facade trace attribution — an undocumented call carries no documentation link; the trace law names it as a dangling call_spec (parity, killed)
kata.series_report: beads catherine-r5k.3 (gap kata, parent catherine-r5k); pre-registered in fixtures/katas/facade/README.md and faults.json. The row has no ploeh §6 grounding: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md listed Facade as disposed (convenience delegation; no invariant); this kata names the strongest expressible delegation law and records the residual gaps.
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the extra call row has no call_spec cell, so totality fires as a dangling call_spec on Call#8; the conventional replay flags the documented-pair multiset as unexpected, naming the same element (parity)

expected.detail: a Call row for f_checkout/a_cart_clear is inserted with call_facade, call_action and call_outcome but no call_spec cell: the declared arrow call_spec has a dangling value at Call#8, which names call:f_checkout/a_cart_clear

expressibility_gap.invariant: the facade's surface is a reduction of the subsystem's (at most as many operations, every promised capability covered)
expressibility_gap.why: there is no cardinality or existential predicate over object rows; equations and keys are row-wise. A facade may also expose a subset by design, so this clause is not an invariant of the pattern and is recorded rather than encoded.

discrepancies: Parity: the undocumented call is named by totality (dangling call_spec) and by the conventional multiset comparison. The unused subsystem capability (a_cart_clear is declared but no entry point documents it) is not a fault: facades may expose a subset, which is why coverage/cardinality is a named gap rather than a rule.
procedure: 1. The law (L1-L6), the fault matrix and their expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/facade/ before the recorded run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/facade_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: the frozen documented multiset of call pairs per entry point, the documented aggregate outcome, and per-call transparency; the sample is exhaustive over all entry points and documented pairs, and the frozen spec is the baseline's own record, never a read-back of the model's SpecCall rows.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: catherine check (violations, key collisions, dangling cells), catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 2 (discovery questions, recorded verbatim and never counted), and catherine query (the fiber/aggregate reachability boundary).

4. Witnesses were mapped to the element vocabulary call:<FacadeOp>/<Action> by their source row (equation/dangling) or key rows; unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements, computed by the baseline script.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique with the executed arm is killed; a probe-silent fault is killed with the missing predicate named, never rewritten as a weaker detection.
